History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
30-year-old active female marathon-trainee presents with 2-week history of activity-related right-knee pain and clicking, likely representing an overuse-related patellofemoral pain syndrome; advised relative rest, continued ice, prescription NSAID, and physiotherapy referral.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Right-knee pain with clicking.  
• Onset – Began ≈ 2 weeks ago after increasing running mileage for marathon training.  
• Course – Pain starts ≈ 20 min into run (~3 mi); sometimes forces patient to stop; resolves with rest/ice; no constant pain at rest.  
• Mechanical symptoms – Audible/palpable clicking during leg-extension/abdominal exercises at gym; no locking, catching, or giving-way.  
• Swelling – Mild transient swelling after initial long run; resolved with ice; no current swelling, redness, or heat.  
• Tingling – Single episode of right-toe tingling post-run; resolved; no ongoing numbness.  
• Aggravating factors – Running > 2–3 mi; leg-extension abdominal exercises.  
• Relieving factors – Rest, ice therapy, occasional ibuprofen 400 mg; transient benefit.  
• Associated symptoms – Denies calf pain, colour/temperature change, fevers, systemic symptoms. Reports occasional lower-leg sock indentation swelling after prolonged standing.  
• Review of systems – Denies back pain; no other joint pain or swelling (hands, feet, elbows, wrists); no GI complaints, asthma, or reflux.

Past Medical History:
• Hyperopia – Treated with LASIK surgery (date not specified).  
• Severe urinary tract infection – Hospitalized/ER visit in past; treated, no ongoing issues.  
• Remote right-knee contusion – Ice-hockey fall “months ago”; bruising only, no known structural injury.  

Past Surgical History:
• LASIK (year not specified).  

Allergies:
• Not documented.  

Medications:
• Ibuprofen 400 mg orally PRN (dose/route/frequency otherwise not documented).  
• Aleve (Naproxen) PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).  

Social History:
• Residence – 60 Sloane Avenue, London.  
• Activity – Regular gym attendance; plays ice-hockey; currently marathon training (running up to 7–8 mi).  
• Tobacco – No conventional cigarette smoking stated; smokes marijuana joints occasionally.  
• Alcohol – Not mentioned.  
• Occupation/finances – Not discussed.

Family History:
• Not elicited.

Physical Examination:
(Virtual – patient-reported/observed findings)  
• General – Appears well; no distress noted on video.  
• Right knee – No visible swelling, erythema, or deformity at rest. Full active flexion and extension without limitation; reports pain only after prolonged running/exercise. No instability testing performed.  
• Left knee – Asymptomatic.  
• Gait – Patient reports normal walking, stair ascent/descent.  
• Calves/feet – No calf tenderness; normal colour/temperature; minimal dependent sock-line indentation after prolonged standing (patient-reported).  
• Vitals – Not provided.

Investigations:
• None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Right-knee pain with clicking, likely overuse injury (probable patellofemoral pain syndrome versus patellar tendinopathy/early meniscal pathology).  
Plan:  
– Continue ice therapy after activity.  
– Relative rest: reduce running mileage/intensity until pain-free.  
– Prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose not specified in transcript) to use regularly WITH FOOD; avoid concurrent ibuprofen.  
– Refer to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment, biomechanics analysis, rehabilitation program.  
– Consider imaging (e.g., MRI) if persistent pain, recurrent swelling, or concerning exam findings on physio review.  
– Red-flag advice: seek urgent care for persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, locking, or inability to flex/extend knee.

Issue 2: Single episode right-toe tingling post-run.  
Plan: Monitor; reassure; no specific intervention needed unless recurrent or progressive.

Issue 3: NSAID use / GI protection.  
Plan: Counsel patient to take NSAID with meals; watch for dyspepsia; consider PPI if prolonged high-dose NSAID required (not explicitly discussed but consistent with standard care—note: no prescription given in transcript).

General follow-up: Telehealth or in-person review if symptoms worsen or fail to improve; routine follow-up after physiotherapy assessment.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Runner’s knee) – High likelihood: activity-related anterior/central knee pain, clicking with flexion/extension, onset after increased mileage, normal ROM, minimal swelling.  
2. Patellar tendinopathy – Moderate likelihood: overuse of extensor mechanism; pain with running/leg-extension; less typical clicking.  
3. Degenerative or traumatic meniscal tear – Moderate likelihood: prior knee trauma and mechanical symptoms; however, no locking or persistent effusion.
